text: Before approval: Testing mode is limited to 100 test users listed on the consent screen.
quote: Projects configured with a publishing status of Testing are limited to up to 100 test users listed in the OAuth consent screen.

text: Before approval: test-user authorizations and refresh tokens expire 7 days after consent.
quote: Authorizations by a test user will expire seven days from the time of consent. If your OAuth client requests an offline access type and receives a refresh token, that token will also expire.

text: Before approval: an In-production app requesting unapproved sensitive or restricted scopes shows the unverified app screen.
quote: Google will display an Unverified apps warning message if your project's OAuth clients request authorization of scopes considered sensitive or restricted before your project has completed verification

text: Before approval: unverified apps are capped at 100 new users for the lifetime of the project, and the cap cannot be reset.
quote: unverified apps that are accessing restricted or sensitive scopes have a 100 new-user cap restriction.
fix: Before approval: unverified apps that request sensitive or restricted scopes are capped at 100 new users for the lifetime of the project, and the cap cannot be reset.
note: Cap applies only to unverified apps accessing sensitive/restricted scopes; claim drops that qualifier. Lifetime/no-reset is stated: "the user cap applies over the entire lifetime of the project, and it cannot be reset or changed."

text: Verify ownership of your authorized domains in Google Search Console.
quote: Verify ownership of your project's authorized domains within the Google Search Console .

text: Host a public home page and a privacy policy on the same domain, both linked from the consent screen.
quote: The privacy policy must be visible to users, hosted within the same domain as your application's home page, and linked to on the OAuth consent screen of the Google API Console.
note: Home page must be publicly accessible; home page URI is part of consent screen branding info.

text: The privacy policy must disclose how the app accesses, uses, stores, or shares Google user data.
quote: The privacy policy must disclose the manner in which your application accesses, uses, stores, or shares Google user data.

text: Give a written justification for each sensitive scope, including why a narrower scope is not enough.
quote: Prepare a detailed justification for each requested sensitive scope, as well as an explanation for why a narrower scope isn't sufficient.

text: Submit an unlisted YouTube video showing the consent flow, the client ID in the address bar, and each scope in use.
quote: Show that the browser address bar of the OAuth consent screen correctly includes your app's OAuth client ID.
note: Page also requires uploading to YouTube with Visibility Unlisted; video must also show the OAuth grant flow and functionality enabled by each sensitive scope.

text: You must publish your branding before you can request verification for data access.
quote: Note that you must have a published branding status before you can request verification for data access.

text: Internal-only apps (Workspace-owned project, Internal audience) skip verification and the 100-user cap but only work in that org.
quote: Your app will not be subject to the unverified app screen or the 100-user cap if it's designated as internal-only.
note: Page also notes the app might need approval from an organization administrator.

text: Google lists reading Google Calendar events as an example of a sensitive scope.
quote: Examples of sensitive scopes include reading events stored in Google Calendar, storing a new contact in Google Contacts, or deleting a YouTube video.

text: No Calendar API scope is on Google's restricted scope list.
quote: The following scopes are categorized as "restricted" Gmail API
note: Restricted list covers only Gmail, Drive, Fit, Chat, Data Portability, Photos Ambient and Google Health APIs; no Calendar scope appears.

text: Narrower scopes such as calendar.events.owned and calendar.freebusy exist if you don't need full calendar access.
quote: https://www.googleapis.com/auth/calendar.events.owned See, create, change, and delete events on Google calendars you own.
note: calendar.freebusy is also listed: "View your availability in your calendars."

text: Google requires you to request the narrowest scope that provides the feature.
quote: You must request the narrowest scope necessary for your app's functionality

text: Google's FAQ estimates sensitive scope verification at 10 business days, which is longer than the 3-5 days on the developer page.
quote: 10 Business days
note: FAQ states 10 business days; the 3-5 day figure is on the developer sensitive-scope page, not this page. FAQ notes estimates are not guaranteed.

text: Limits apply to refresh tokens: 100 per Google Account per client ID, and creating a new one silently invalidates the oldest.
quote: If the limit is reached, creating a new refresh token automatically invalidates the oldest refresh token without warning.

text: Refresh tokens stop working after 6 months unused or if the user revokes access.
quote: The user has revoked your app's access . The refresh token has not been used for six months.
note: Page lists further reasons too (password change with Gmail scopes, token limit, time-based access, admin policy).

text: Your OAuth redirect URI must exactly match oauth_redirect_uri in the Composio auth config; some defaults still use /api/v1/auth-apps/add.
quote: The redirect URI in your OAuth app must exactly match oauth_redirect_uri in your Composio auth config. Some toolkit defaults still use https://backend.composio.dev/api/v1/auth-apps/add

text: Use separate Google Cloud projects for testing and production, and submit only the production project for verification.
quote: You should only submit “production” tier projects for verification.

text: Workspace admins can restrict sensitive scopes to OAuth clients they explicitly mark as trusted.
quote: Google Workspace organization administrators might restrict access to sensitive scopes to prevent access by OAuth client IDs that the organization doesn't explicitly mark as trusted.

text: Google OAuth sensitive scope verification (includes brand verification) | wait: 3-5 business days (Google's FAQ estimates 10)
quote: Note that your app might be eligible to complete brand verification as a subset of your sensitive scope verification request.
fix: Google OAuth sensitive scope verification (branding must be published first) | wait: typically 3-5 business days
note: Page says verification "typically takes 3-5 business days"; brand verification "might" be a subset and that published branding is required before requesting data access verification; the FAQ 10-day estimate is not on this page.

text: Before approval: a custom-distribution app installs only on one store, stores in one Plus organization, or development stores.
quote: Custom distribution Installed on a single Shopify store, on multiple stores that belong to the same Plus organization, or on development stores

text: Before approval: protected customer data needs no review only while the app is installed solely on development stores.
quote: You don't need to submit a request for review for apps that are installed only on development stores.
fix: Before approval: a public app can use protected customer data without review only while installed solely on development stores; custom apps get level 1 and 2 access without review.
note: Page table shows protected customer data is "Always available" (no review) for custom apps, so "only" while on dev stores is overstated.

text: Public apps must request protected customer data access, and level 1 and 2 access requires review.
quote: Level Public app Custom app Admin created custom app 1 Requires review Always available Always available 2 Requires review Always available Varies by plan
fix: Public apps that use protected customer data must request access, and level 1 and 2 access requires review.
note: Level 0 (no customer data) requires no action, so not every public app must request access.

text: App Store apps must subscribe to the customers/data_request, customers/redact and shop/redact compliance webhooks.
quote: Every app that's distributed through the Shopify App Store must subscribe to the following compliance webhook topics:

text: New public apps must be built only with the GraphQL Admin API.
quote: As of April 1, 2025 all new public apps must be built exclusively with the GraphQL Admin API .

text: Review submissions need a screencast, working test credentials and an emergency developer contact.
quote: 4.5.6 Provide an emergency developer contact. Add an emergency developer contact to your Partner Dashboard.

text: The app must authenticate with OAuth immediately after install, before any other step.
quote: 2.3.2 Authenticate immediately after install. Your app must immediately authenticate using OAuth before any other steps occur.

text: App charges must go through Shopify App Pricing or the Billing API.
quote: Your app must use Shopify App Pricing or the Shopify Billing API for any app charges.

text: Composio has no managed Shopify app, so you must bring your own credentials.
quote: Authentication Details Composio-managed OAuth not available OAuth2 S2S_OAUTH2

text: New public apps must use expiring offline tokens that last 1 hour, with refresh tokens valid 90 days.
quote: Expiring offline access token 1 hour ( expires_in is 3600 ) Refresh token for an expiring offline access token 90 days ( refresh_token_expires_in is 7776000 ) when issued.
note: Requirement applies to GraphQL Admin API requests; page notes refreshing can shorten the refresh token lifetime.

text: You cannot change the distribution method after you select it.
quote: You can't change the distribution method after you select it.

text: Composio asks for the store subdomain (e.g. je0xpi-12) when connecting an account.
quote: Store subdomain: Enter your Shopify store's subdomain. If your store URL is https://je0xpi-12.myshopify.com , enter je0xpi-12

text: Order updates can 403 without the read_all_orders scope.
quote: Shopify order update 403s can be caused by missing read_all_orders scope
note: FAQ answer rendered via Playwright.

text: Shopify App Store review (public distribution), plus protected customer data review if you read customer data | wait: not stated
quote: Public distribution also requires registering for the Shopify App Store, which has a one-time fee.
fix: Public distribution requires Shopify approval and Shopify App Store registration | wait: not stated
note: Distribution page confirms approval is required for public distribution and gives no wait time, but does not mention a protected customer data review (that is on the protected-customer-data page).

text: One-time $19 USD App Store registration fee per Partner account
quote: you need to register with the Shopify App Store for a one-time fee of $19 USD per Partner account.

text: Without approval, only open permissions work: profile, email (OpenID Connect) and w_member_social.
quote: Open Permissions are the only permissions that are available to all developers without special approval.
note: Open permissions listed: profile and email (Sign in with LinkedIn using OpenID Connect) and w_member_social (Share on LinkedIn).

text: Community Management Development tier allows 500 requests per app and 100 per member.
quote: Per App : Increased from 100 to 500 requests. Per Member : Increased from 10 to 100 requests.

text: Rate limits are daily, reset at midnight UTC, and are not published; check the app's Analytics tab.
quote: Standard rate limits are not published in documentation.
note: Page says to look them up in the Developer Portal app Analytics tab.

text: Redirect URLs must be absolute HTTPS URLs with no # fragment.
quote: URLs cannot include a # https://dev.example.com/auth/linkedin/callback#linkedin is invalid.
note: Page says "Add the redirect (callback) URL via HTTPS to your server."

text: Creating the app asks for an app name, a Company page URL and a logo.
quote: enter the basic required app details, like the App name, Company page URL, and the logo that users will see when they authorize with your app.

text: Self-serve products are added from the Products tab of the app.
quote: Select your app from My Apps , navigate to the Products tab, and add the Share on LinkedIn product which will grant you w_member_social .

text: Standard tier requests need a screencast showing each use case.
quote: When applying for Standard Tier, provide a screencast video demonstrating each use case specified in your access request form

text: Access tokens last 60 days; programmatic refresh tokens are for approved Marketing Developer Platform partners.
quote: By default, access tokens are valid for 60 days and programmatic refresh tokens are valid for a year.

text: Changing an app's scopes means users must re-authenticate.
quote: If the scope permissions are changed in your app, your users must re-authenticate

text: Composio's organization tools need w_organization_social or rw_organization_admin, which are not open permissions.
quote: w_organization_social scope for posting as an organization (with ADMINISTRATOR, DIRECT_SPONSORED_CONTENT_POSTER, or CONTENT_ADMIN role)
fix: Composio's LinkedIn organization tools need w_organization_social to post as an organization, rw_organization_admin for page and share statistics, and r_organization_admin for company info.
note: Quote is from tool metadata embedded in the page HTML (shown when a tool is expanded). Per that metadata, GET_COMPANY_INFO needs r_organization_admin (not in the claim); the Composio page does not say these are not open permissions (that comes from LinkedIn's getting-access page).

text: w_member_social and r_organization_admin cannot be used together.
quote: LinkedIn restricts certain scope combinations. For example, w_member_social and r_organization_admin cannot be used together.
note: FAQ answer rendered via Playwright.

text: Community Management access must be requested on a new app with no other API products.
quote: Only request Community Management API Development Tier access with new developer applications that don't have access to other API products.

text: r_member_social is closed and LinkedIn is not accepting requests for it.
quote: r_member_social is a closed permission. We're not accepting access requests at this time due to resource constraints.

text: OAuth apps get 5,000 requests and 2,000,000 complexity points per hour per user or app user.
quote: OAuth App 5,000 User (or App User) 1 hour

text: Configure your redirect callback URLs on the app; the token exchange must use the same redirect_uri.
quote: redirect_uri (required) Same redirect URI which you used in the previous step

text: Linear highly recommends creating a dedicated workspace to own the OAuth app.
quote: It is highly recommended you create a workspace for the purpose of managing the OAuth2 Application, as each admin user will have access.

text: Directory listings are for useful integrations built by formal companies, not hobby or low-effort apps.
quote: We'll accept integrations that we think are useful to the community and are built by formal companies. We generally do not accept scripts, low-effort/vibe coded or apps built by hobbyists

text: A directory listing needs a submission form, 320x320 color and white icons, and 1-3 showcase images at 1600x1000.
quote: Showcase images (1-3 max) 1600px x 1000px in .svg, .jpeg, or .png file format

text: Authorization-code access tokens are valid for 24 hours and come with a refresh token.
quote: a valid access token and refresh token will be returned in the response. The access token is valid for 24 hours

text: All OAuth apps were moved to the refresh token system on April 1, 2026.
quote: All OAuth2 applications were migrated to the new refresh token system on April 1, 2026.

text: Each refresh returns a new access and refresh token; a lost response can be replayed within 30 minutes.
quote: you can replay the original request to retrieve the new refresh token up to 30 minutes after the original request.

text: actor=app creates resources as the app instead of the authorizing user.
quote: app - Resources are created as the application.
note: Default actor=user creates resources as the authorizing user.

text: Request the admin scope only when absolutely necessary.
quote: admin - Full access to admin level endpoints. You should never ask for this permission unless it's absolutely needed

text: Every admin of the workspace that owns the app can access the app's settings.
quote: It is highly recommended you create a workspace for the purpose of managing the OAuth2 Application, as each admin user will have access.

text: Limit of 10 simultaneous connections per user; there is no way to raise it.
quote: Currently there are no options to raise the limit on a per-customer basis. Throttling The Marketing API has a limit of 10 simultaneous connections.

text: API calls time out after 120 seconds.
quote: The Marketing API has a 120-second timeout on API calls.

text: Some Composio Mailchimp tools need at least the Essentials plan.
quote: Some Mailchimp API/tool capabilities require at least the Mailchimp Essentials plan.
note: FAQ answer rendered via Playwright.

text: Register the app on the Registered Apps page in your Mailchimp account.
quote: Navigate to the Registered Apps page in your Mailchimp account Click Register An App

text: HTTPS for the redirect URI is strongly recommended but not enforced.
quote: For security, we strongly recommend—but do not enforce—using HTTPS for your redirect_uri .

text: Delete stored tokens when a user disconnects or uninstalls your app.
quote: when a user disconnects or uninstalls your application, delete the access token you stored for them

text: The client secret is shown only once at registration.
quote: This is the only time you'll be able to see client_secret , so you'll need to copy it and store it securely.
note: A rotated secret is likewise shown only once.

text: Access tokens never expire and there is no refresh token.
quote: Mailchimp access tokens have no expiry, so there is no refresh_token and nothing to rotate on a schedule.

text: A token is revoked if the authorizing user is removed from the account.
quote: If that user is removed from the account, the token is revoked.

text: API access is bounded by the authorizing user's role; use an admin where possible.
quote: When creating a key or authorizing an app, use an admin user where you can.
